newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt readies new budget to meet EMU terms.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt readies new budget to meet EMU terms.

text.p: Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi and Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi have worked out a framework for a new budget to ensure Italy is a founder member of the single European currency, the prime minister's office said in a statement on Wednesday.
It said the package, to be based on structural measures, would be launched in the coming weeks, as soon as the Treasury knew how much money had to be raised.
"This budget, tied to progress already made, will allow Italy to meet the necessary objectives needed to fully satisfy the Maastricht Treaty," the statement said.

It added that the package would mean that Italy could adhere to the stability pact, agreed last year by European Union leaders, which establishes strict economic guidelines for members of European economic and monetary union (EMU).

Italy introduced a 62.5 trillion lire budget at the end of last year as it made a last gasp bid to be part of EMU from its planned launch in 1999, but figures showing a sharp overshoot in 1996 spending blew a fresh hole in state accounts.

Financial newspaper Il Sole 24 Ore quoted Treasury sources earlier this month as saying that 15.0 trillion lire of additional budgetary measures would be needed to meet government targets and tame the public sector deficit.
